text.tspan: User
a person, or another agent
Conversation
the thing you look at: a durable transcript with an id
Query
one say and everything it caused, until it closes
Turn
one round of the model loop
Message
an utterance in the transcript, with a stable id
Content block
text, thinking, tool use, tool result, image, document
Ref
a heavy block stored by content hash, fetched on demand
Tip
which message the conversation currently stands at
World
a place an agent can run: a machine, a container
Agent instance
one process's presence in a world: (world, instanceId)
Attachment
the claim: this instance is serving this conversation, now
Approval
a pending ask: may the agent do this thing

g.text: Derived by each reader, never stored as a verdict

text.tspan: Read it as a sentence. A user says into a conversation; the say opens a query; the query runs turns until the model stops asking for tools; each turn commits messages, made of content blocks, with the heavy ones swapped for refs the client fetches only if it needs them.

The conversation is entirely separate from where it runs. An agent instance is a process's presence in a world, and the only link between the two sides is the attachment: a claim that this instance is serving this conversation, now. At most one stands at a time, a new one unconditionally supersedes the last, and that supersession is exactly what migrating a conversation to another machine is.

Nothing declares whether an instance is alive or a conversation is stale. Both are folds each reader computes for itself from the events it has seen, so there is no verdict to go wrong and no server tick to depend on.
Colours: gold = people, blue = the conversation, cyan = what it is made of, orange = placement, purple = the claim, red = permission, dashed = derived, never stored.
Liveness
alive · released · stranded, from the last pulse against the reader's own clock
Staleness
how long since this conversation moved; what orders the fleet

g.text: has many: the loop runs until the model stops asking for tools

text.tspan: lives in, and one or many share a world;
the pair (world, instanceId) is the instance's whole identity

g.text: claims; at most one stands at a time
asking a different world to serve is how work migrates
